question:
A 77-year-old female with multiple comorbidities including mild Alzheimer dementia, hypertension, type
2 diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, and atrial fibrillation (treated with apixaban) is admitted to the
hospital for pneumonia. She presents with fatigue, fever (37.9°C), decreased oxygen saturation (85%
on room air), elevated leukocyte count (12,300/mm3), and radiographic evidence of right lower lobe
consolidation. Prior to admission, she lived with her son and required minimal standby assistance for
ADLs, walking independently despite occasional unsteadiness due to impulsivity and poor safety
awareness. She has experienced two falls in the past year. During her first night of hospitalization, she
makes frequent unsupervised attempts to get out of bed, primarily for toileting. Beyond providing
toileting assistance, which of the following interventions would be most effective in reducing her fall risk

during this hospital stay? Answer Choices: (A) Transfer the patient to a room closer to the nursing
station (B) Consult physical therapy, and place a mobility order that she ambulate with assistance
around the hospital floor at least three times daily (C) Install a bedside commode and implement hourly
rounding (D) Start a scheduled antipsychotic medication for delirium prevention (E) Place an external
female catheter to reduce the need for getting out of bed to go to the bathroom (F) Implement a
scheduled toileting program every 2 hours (G) Place the patient in four-point soft restraints during
nighttime hours (H) Place fall precaution signage and non-slip socks (I) Request that the nursing staff
use a bed alarm (J) Prescribe as-needed benzodiazepines for nighttime agitation
 A. Place the patient in four-point soft restraints during nighttime hours
B. Start a scheduled antipsychotic medication for delirium prevention
C. Place an external female catheter to reduce the need for getting out of bed to go to the bathroom
D. Implement a scheduled toileting program every 2 hours
E. Consult physical therapy, and place a mobility order that she ambulate with assistance around
the hospital floor at least three times daily
F. Place fall precaution signage and non-slip socks
G. Install a bedside commode and implement hourly rounding
H. Transfer the patient to a room closer to the nursing station
I. Prescribe as-needed benzodiazepines for nighttime agitation
J. Request that the nursing staff use a bed alarm
